verdict: The hub reads as a prototype, not a polished menu: the room labels are all the same size and weight, the top HUD text is tiny and scattered, and a capital letter, an explaining sentence and a clipped caption sit next to the player.

findings.where: the last pour label and its caption
findings.what: The line '***experimental feature may glitch***' is an explaining sentence with asterisks. It is set in a different, thin face, is crushed against the 'the last pour' label, and overlaps NPC sprites. It is also clipped by the station circle below it.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. If a flag is needed, use a 16px f-cond tag 'experimental' in --warn on a --ui-panel chip, 8px below the label, with no asterisks.

findings.where: top-left title block 'the undercroft / 0 items in stash · 0 runs'
findings.what: The title is about 20px amber and sits against the screen corner. The subline is about 12px, below the 14px floor, and is cut off at the edge of the dark side bar ('0 runs' touches the frame). It is not an accent colour from the guide, it has no panel, and nothing gives the screen a clear title.
findings.fix: Place the title at x=48, y=40 (the 5% margin) in f-cond 700 32px --tx-1. Put the subline below it in 16px --tx-2 with 8px between. Keep the 'stash' figures out of this block, since they repeat in the top right.

findings.what: There are three groups of different sizes and weights ($900 bold about 22px, '0 xp' with a tiny 'xp', and 'stash $0 bag $0' about 14px). They sit in a horizontal row with uneven gaps and no panel, and they drift over the dark void. This ignores the owner's vertical 1x1 list order, so the money figure does not read as the hero number.
findings.fix: Switch to the cw-trcol vertical list: every row 20px f-cond 600, label in --tx-2 at 16px, value in --tx-1 right-aligned, 8px row gap, 48px from the right edge. Use one --ui-panel at 90% with 1px --ui-line-hi.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, enter raid!, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, the last pour, fashion)
findings.what: All eight labels use the same size (~36px) and weight inside black boxes. 'enter raid!' is the main action but has no more weight than 'settings', and it carries an exclamation mark. The 36px size is outside the five-step scale. The boxes are different widths, with uneven padding, and they overlap NPCs and pillars ('the stash' is cut by an NPC head).
findings.fix: Make secondary labels 20px f-cond 600 --tx-1 on --ui-panel, with 8px/16px padding and a 4px radius. Make 'enter raid' the one 32px label with a 2px lime (--acc) top tab, and drop the '!'. Add a 3px --ui-void halo or move the labels out so they do not cover NPCs.

findings.where: bottom centre: 'in pillager's party' chip and 'l stick walk · ls jog · a use station' legend
findings.what: The legend is about 12px, light text on a busy scene with no panel, and sits on top of the stash desk. The chip is a different size from every other label. 'in pillager's party' is stacked above the legend with no spacing logic, and both are squeezed against the hotbar. Contrast of the legend is poor.
findings.fix: Put the legend in a --ui-panel strip at 16px f-cond --tx-2 with key glyphs in --tx-1, centred 16px above the hotbar. Move the party chip to the top-left under the title, so it is a status, not a floating tooltip.

findings.what: The hotbar is a game-HUD element in the hub. It uses nine equal slots of dark grey weapon silhouettes at very low contrast. The selected slot is a thin amber outline, not the lime accent. Slot numbers are about 12px and sit apart from the icons. It also takes the whole bottom strip over the playfield.
findings.fix: Reduce the hub row to the slots that hold something. Use a --acc 2px border and --ui-raised fill for the focused slot. Raise the slot numbers to 16px --tx-2 and the empty icons to at least 4.5:1.

findings.where: player tags ('pillager' in amber, ring badges 1 and 2)
findings.what: The 'pillager' name tag is amber on the dark floor, near the 'fashion' label. P1 and P2 are told apart only by the small ring badges at about 14px, and the P2 marker is partly hidden behind P1 and the 'fashion' label. The tag has no panel or alignment with the other labels.
findings.fix: Draw the name tag at 16px f-cond in --tx-1 on a --ui-panel chip centred 8px above the head, with a 24px ring badge. Do not change ring colours until the owner picks P1 and P2 colours.

findings.what: The device chip is about 14px with a green outline that matches no token. It sits against the top frame, close to 'enter raid!', and the lowest-priority item is thus the highest on the screen. The pillar sprites behind it add noise.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond --tx-2 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, and 24px from the top. Drop the green outline.
